entities.summary:
DreamWorks Animation (DreamWorks SKG, founded 1994) is a major Hollywood studio founded by Steven Spielberg, Jeffrey Katzenberg, and David Geffen — three of the most powerful figures in entertainment history — whose combined initials gave the studio its 'SKG' suffix. DreamWorks represented the last successful attempt to create an independent Hollywood major studio, producing Saving Private Ryan (1998), American Beauty (1999, Best Picture), Gladiator (2000, Best Picture), and the Shrek and Madagascar animated franchises.

The studio's founding in 1994 was Hollywood's most anticipated event in decades: Spielberg left Universal, Katzenberg left Disney (after a bitter lawsuit), and music mogul Geffen contributed $1 billion each to launch a studio with no major corporate owner. The combination of Spielberg's directorial genius, Katzenberg's animation expertise (he had supervised The Little Mermaid, Beauty and the Beast, The Lion King at Disney), and Geffen's music industry relationships created extraordinary buzz.

DreamWorks Animation spun off as a separate company in 2004; the live-action studio was acquired by Paramount in 2006 for $1.6 billion; DreamWorks Animation was acquired by NBCUniversal/Comcast in 2016 for $3.8 billion. Shrek (2001) won the first Academy Award for Best Animated Feature Film. The studio's independence was ultimately unsustainable against major studios' distribution infrastructure, but its 12-year independent run produced some of the most acclaimed films of the 1990s-2000s.
